fixes.explanation: That's the point, friend. Paul asks, "If God is for us, who can be against us?" (Romans 8:31). He isn't saying no one will ever oppose us. He's saying no one can win against us when God is on our side. Picture a crowd of opponents who all take one look at who's standing behind us and suddenly find something to do in the other room.

Nothing in Paul's question asks us to earn anything. He just says, "If God is for us…" and he doesn't add a single condition after it (Romans 8:31). Paul even says God "did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all" (Romans 8:32). God is for us, and that settles who can be against us.

Not quite, and this one is easy to trip on. Paul asks, "Who is there to condemn us?" and then points to Christ Jesus, who died, was raised to life, and is at the right hand of God (Romans 8:34). Paul says that Jesus "is interceding for us." So Jesus is not the one condemning. He's speaking up for us.

I see why you'd think so, but look at the list again. Trouble, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger, sword (Romans 8:35). Paul lists hard things people suffer, and the next verse says "we face death all day long" (Romans 8:36). I think Paul wants us to see that even the hardest things we face can't separate us from the love of Christ.

Israel is a fair guess, but Paul's list is bigger than any one nation. He writes, "…nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God…" (Romans 8:39). Creation is the word he lands on. Everything God made falls under it, and none of it can cut us off from that love.
